title: End-to-end latency & throughput study for FP8/INT8 calibration regimens with KV-cache and batching at long context
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Purpose:
This ticket coordinates an end-to-end benchmark that quantifies throughput and latency trade-offs introduced by different FP8 and INT8 calibration regimens under production-like batching and KV-cache behavior with long context lengths. The aim is to produce a reproducible matrix of results that ties calibration choices to measurable user-facing SLOs and to validate accuracy regressions relative to the FP32 baseline.

Background:
Previous experiments focused on small contexts or offline calibration artifacts; we still lack a systematic comparison of: (a) per-layer vs per-channel calibration, (b) static (one-shot) vs iterative calibration passes, (c) calibration dataset size/selection, and (d) interaction with runtime features: KV cache warm/cold behavior and continuous/dynamic batching. Teams have observed non-intuitive latency tails when mixing INT8 kernels and dynamic batching, particularly on long horizons (>8k tokens).

Goals / Hypotheses:
- Quant profiles that minimize accuracy delta (<= 0.5% relative to FP32 on our eval set) can be found that still deliver 25-40% throughput gains for 7B/13B models with typical batching patterns.
- INT8 calibrated with per-channel ranges will have lower accuracy variance across prompts but potentially higher calibration cost than layer-wise FP8 recipes.
- KV cache warm vs cold states significantly change tail latency; calibration-induced kernel selection differences may disproportionately affect P95/P99 latency.
- Adaptive batching combined with conservative quant-fallback rules reduces P99 regressions at modest throughput cost.

Planned experiments (high level):
- Models: 7B, 13B, 70B (representative family picks used in runtime-1.20 catalog)
- Context lengths: 2048, 8192, 32768 (to capture medium and long-horizon behavior)
- Batch sizes: 1, 4, 16 (and a simulated dynamic batching mix derived from production trace)
- KV-cache states: cold (no cached KV), warm (prepopulated from a 128-token prefix), rolling (hot segments interleaved with cold requests)
- Calibration regimens:
  * FP8 per-layer static (one-shot) using 2k and 10k calibration samples
  * FP8 per-channel iterative (3 passes with sample shuffling)
  * INT8 symmetric per-channel calibration (linear-tied/affine) with min-max and KL divergence calibration variants
  * Hybrid: FP8 activations + INT8 weights where supported
- Metrics to capture: median latency, P95, P99, tokens/sec (steady-state and cold-start), CPU/GPU utilization, model accuracy metrics (perplexity, downstream classification F1 on standard eval prompts), and per-token output divergence (BLEU-like or edit distance where applicable).

Acceptance criteria for candidate quant profile to consider for rollout:
- Median latency improvement >= 20% vs FP32 for the same batching config AND P99 degradation <= 10% (absolute) compared to FP32 P99; OR
- Tokens/sec improvement >= 25% with accuracy regression <= 0.5% on the validated eval set.
- No reproducible correctness regressions on critical safety/eval prompts.

Artifacts and links (working):
- Benchmark spec & runbook (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/ENG-48902+Quant+Benchmark+Runbook
- Calib pipeline code (draft): https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/tree/ENG-48902
- Notebook with initial eval harness and sample selection: https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/blob/main/eng-48902-calib-notebook.ipynb
- Dashboard (Grafana snapshot) for first run: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/bench/eng-48902
- PR (draft) for runtime kernel selection guard rails: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1723

Notes on reproducibility:
- All experiments will be launched via the in-house bench-runner with pinned seeds and container images. Calibration artifacts (scale tables, histogram logs) will be persisted to S3 under s3://redwood-inference/bench/ENG-48902 for later audit.
- We will run each cell of the matrix 3 times and report mean + standard deviation; if SD of P99 > 6% for a configuration, we will increase runs to 7 to reduce noise.

Why this differs from earlier tickets:
- Focuses on end-to-end production interaction (batching + KV-cache) rather than isolated quant math microbenchmarks.
- Explicitly compares calibration regimen cost (time + sample size) to latency/throughput benefits and captures repeatability under dynamic workloads.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Calibration with large sample sets (10k+) is costly and may slow release cadence; we will record wall-time and compute cost per regimen.
- Hybrid quantization introduces operational complexity for kernel selection and fallback; guard rails must be conservative.
- Long-context experiments are expensive (GPU memory/time). We will prioritize 13B and simulate 70B via sequence-slicing for initial runs if needed.
acceptance_criteria: Median latency improvement >= 20% OR tokens/sec improvement >= 25% vs FP32 with accuracy regression <= 0.5%; P99 degradation bounded as described; no safety/eval failures

updates: 2025-02-18: Ticket created by Ava Patel; initial scoping and high-level matrix recorded.

2025-02-21: First calibration runner prototype committed (branch eng-48902-calib). Noted non-deterministic histogram buckets when using asynchronous sample loader.

2025-02-22: Resolved loader non-determinism (seeded shuffling + deterministic minibatch ordering). Re-ran a 7B/2k context pilot: measured tokens/sec +5% for FP8-layer-static but P99 increased by 18% in dynamic batching mix.

2025-02-24: Post-mortem on P99 spike: correlated spikes with kernel fallback on a specific attention kernel under 13B INT8 path. Opened PR runtime/pull/1723 to add conservative kernel fallback on P99-sensitive routes.
2025-02-26: Running expanded matrix for 7B and 13B with calibrated kernels disabled (control) to measure baseline kernel fallback frequency. Infrastructure cost estimate updated in Confluence.

2025-02-28: Interim summary: FP8 per-channel iterative regimen shows lower accuracy variance but needs 3x more calibration compute. Next: run the 8k context cells and then collect full 3-run statistics for 7B/13B. Assigned Diego and Mei (measurement lead) to finalize aggregation scripts.
